{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Legal review of the Master Services Agreement against our playbook

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The commercial architecture of the deal is broadly acceptable — the liability cap, licence grant, warranty package, assignment rights, audit rights, renewal mechanics and Vendor insurance all sit at our preferred position and require no redline. The problem is concentrated in two places: (i) a set of one-way restrictive covenants and commitments imposed on us, and (ii) material omissions.

The single most serious issue is that the Agreement contains **no indemnity at all**. There is no Section 20, yet four separate clauses (§ 9.3, § 19.4, § 21.3, § 30.5) cross-refer to indemnities as if one existed — including § 9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" for IP infringement remedies. We have no defence or hold-harmless protection for third-party IP claims, and the drafting is internally broken.

Separately, § 12.4 (which appears twice), § 7.2 and § 2.1 load us with a three-year USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights", a worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete, a 24-month no-hire covering *all* Vendor employees, and an open-ended duty to disclose and match any better third-party offer. Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and each directly contradicts § 12.3, in which the Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. That internal contradiction is our strongest negotiating lever: we are asking the Vendor to conform the operative text to a representation it has already made.

We also have no termination-for-convenience right across a three-year term, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return mechanic, Vendor ownership of Deliverables we pay for, and a Singapore governing law clause that conflicts with the New York venue clause immediately beneath it (§ 28.1 vs § 28.2).

In total: 19 findings — 9 deviations or omissions requiring redlines, 10 compliant provisions requiring no action.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No § 20 (cross-refs at § 9.3, § 19.4, § 21.3, § 30.5; disclaimer at § 19.5) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless clause exists anywhere, despite four clauses presupposing one. Below fallback and in walk-away territory. We insert a Section 20 at the preferred position (IP, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies numbered 20.5 to restore the § 9.3 cross-reference, a standard claim procedure, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for us; we get only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. Fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense). The § 13.2 perpetual licence does not cure the gap — it reaches only Vendor Technology delivered paid-up or embedded in a Deliverable. Redline reverses the assignment while preserving Vendor background IP and the embedded-IP licence. Customer Data ownership (§ 14.1), Vendor Technology retention (§ 14.3) and no joint ownership (§ 14.4) are satisfactory. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second instance) | Bars us from developing or acquiring any competing product or service, in any territory, for the term plus 24 months, with no category limit and no performance exit — exclusive dealing in walk-away territory and well beyond the fallback. Contradicts § 12.3. Redline deletes the covenant and confirms Vendor is non-exclusive. |
| 4 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete sweeping in acquisitions and internal development. Fails the fallback on every material term (post-term duration exceeds 12 months; scope unlimited; no carve-outs) and is walk-away. Contradicts § 12.3. Preferred position: delete; narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, with carve-outs) offered in comment. |
| 5 | High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way true no-hire ("hire, or employ") covering *every* Vendor employee for 24 months post-term, expressly overriding general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs. Fails the fallback (mutual, involved personnel, 12 months, with carve-outs, no no-hire) on every material term; walk-away because it is a no-hire across all personnel. Contradicts § 12.3. Redline deletes; narrow mutual 12-month fallback offered in comment. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (§ 9.1–9.3 only); § 2.1; § 8.1 | Only for-cause, insolvency and security/service-level termination rights exist. No convenience right anywhere across a three-year term, and § 2.1 locks us in "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away. We insert § 9.4 at the preferred position (30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right), expressly overriding § 2.1. Vendor has no convenience right today, so no deletion is needed on its side. |
| 7 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | The MFN runs against us: we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive, with no product limitation, no time limit and no comparison carve-outs. Walk-away position; fails the fallback (defined product, 12-month cap, reasonable-comparison exceptions). Contradicts § 12.3. Redline deletes § 7.2. |
| 8 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — walk-away, and beyond the fallback (current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice with true-up rather than penalty). Conflicts with § 12.3 and with the § 9 termination rights. Preferred position: no minimum commitment; pay only for Services used or ordered, consistent with § 7.1. |
| 9 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (conflicts with § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and effectively the walk-away case of exclusive foreign venue. It also directly conflicts with § 28.2, which gives exclusive jurisdiction to state and federal courts in New York County. Redline replaces only the jurisdiction and forum words in § 28.1 with New York, aligning the two clauses; § 28.3 escalation untouched. |
| 10 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1, § 10.2, § 16.5, § 15 | No post-termination transition-assistance or data-return obligation. § 10.1 assumes "any agreed transition period" without creating a right to one; § 10.2 covers only Deliverables and refunds; § 16.5's return-or-destroy duty carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" — there is no Section 11, and Section 15 addresses only processing restrictions and privacy compliance, not return, format or deletion timing. Neither preferred nor fallback met. We insert § 10.3: up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, machine-readable return of Customer Data within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter (with the customary backup/legal-retention carve-out already used in § 16.5). Ninety days' assistance available as fallback. |
| 11 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1–21.4 (see also § 1.5, § 18.2) | At preferred position. Mutual cap at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion that confirms restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages; carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement; severability of caps on failure of exclusive remedy. Fee base is substantive; exclusion of the one-time implementation charge is immaterial given the USD 1,000,000 floor. No redline. |
| 12 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1–24.4 (see also § 13.3) | At preferred position and favourable to us: Affiliate/M&A assignment by us on notice only; Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance or transfer by change of control without our consent and never to a direct competitor; mutual reasonableness standard elsewhere; and no Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate or reduce services on our change of control. No redline. |
| 13 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 (see also § 7.3, § 10.2, § 21.1, § 27.3) | No liquidated damages, penalty, termination fee or acceleration payable by us. § 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use or similar charges; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately not due; § 27.3 permits force-majeure termination "without penalty". Preferred position met. The § 2.1 take-or-pay is addressed under MINCOMMIT and not double-flagged. |
| 14 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1–13.4 | At preferred position: grant extends to Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf with no notice precondition; § 13.2 gives a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid licence to delivered software and Vendor Technology (including Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable); § 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor and bars revocation or suspension except for material uncured payment or use breach after notice and cure. § 13.4 restrictions are ordinary and carved back for lawful testing and Customer Data. The § 14.2 Deliverable licence outlier is addressed under IP (finding 2), not double-flagged. |
| 15 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1–22.3 (see also § 23) | At preferred position: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor under confidentiality; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%; no direct system access and no access to unrelated Customer Data, privileged material or other suppliers' confidential information; findings are our Confidential Information and the final report must be shared. § 23 is a heading with no substantive text. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | At preferred position: 12-month renewal terms (no multi-year auto-renewal), 30-day non-renewal window for us, 60-day Vendor reminder with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is not sent, and uplifts capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% on 90 days' notice with no increase on prepaid periods. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1–19.5 (see also § 6.2) | At preferred position: professional and workmanlike services warranty plus conformity to documentation and specifications; 90-day Deliverable conformity and continuous conformity for hosted Services throughout the subscription term; malicious-code and Applicable Law warranties; re-performance/repair/replacement with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. No "AS IS" language; § 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and does not swallow the express warranties. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1–18.2 | At preferred position and above fallback: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, statutory workers' compensation, employer's liability USD 1M, E&O USD 2M, cyber and privacy USD 5M, maintained for the term plus one year; certificates on request, primacy, cancellation notice, and confirmation that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under our playbook. We should not sign without resolution of each.

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing § 20).** No IP, legal-compliance, data-breach or misconduct indemnity exists, while § 9.3, § 19.4, § 21.3 and § 30.5 all assume one does. We must have a Section 20 with IP remedies numbered 20.5 to make § 9.3 operable.
2. **Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1).** Multi-year lock-in with no reduction or exit mechanism.
3. **No termination for convenience across the three-year term (§ 9, § 8.1).** Compounded by the § 2.1 no-termination language.
4. **Worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete on us (§ 12.4).** Undefined scope, sweeping in acquisitions and internal development.
5. **Exclusive-dealing covenant (second § 12.4).** Term plus 24 months, all territories, no category limit, no performance-based exit.
6. **One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees (§ 12.4).** Overrides general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
7. **Customer-side MFN / duty to disclose and match (§ 7.2).** Open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor.
8. **Exclusive Singapore governing law and jurisdiction (§ 28.1).** Outside the accepted list, and in direct conflict with § 28.2.

Items 2 through 7 each contradict § 12.3, in which the Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. We should present them as a single conforming package.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline with the § 12.3 conflict up front.** Lead the cover note with § 12.3 and ask the Vendor to conform § 2.1, § 7.2 and both instances of § 12.4 to the acknowledgement it has already given. This is a consistency argument, not a concession request, and is the cheapest path to five of the eight walk-away items.
2. **Insert Section 20 (Indemnification) as drafted.** Flag that § 9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" is currently a dead reference and that our numbering restores it; this is presented as a drafting repair as well as a substantive ask.
3. **Add § 9.4 (termination for convenience)** — 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no reciprocal Vendor right — with an express override of § 2.1.
4. **Reverse § 14.2 Deliverable ownership** to us with Vendor assignment, expressly preserving Vendor background IP and the § 13.2 embedded-IP licence. Fallback if resisted: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.
5. **Insert § 10.3 (transition and data return)** — up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, certified deletion with the § 16.5 backup/legal-retention carve-out. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. Note separately that § 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11 and needs correcting.
6. **Amend § 28.1** to New York law and New York County courts, aligning it with § 28.2 and leaving § 28.3 escalation intact.
7. **Confirm no further movement is sought** on the liability cap, assignment, licence grant, warranty, audit, renewal, insurance and no-LD provisions. These sit at our preferred position and we should protect them in any horse-trading.
8. **Escalate the two commercial items** — the § 2.1 volume commitment and the § 12.4 restrictive covenants — to the business owner before the next negotiation session, so we know our authority on the fallbacks (12-month reducible commitment with true-up; narrowed term-only non-compete; mutual 12-month non-solicit).

*This memo is based solely on the verified findings listed above. Section references are as they appear in the Agreement, including the duplicate numbering at § 12.4 and the missing Sections 11 and 20.*"}
